task.title: balanced-brackets
task.statement: The brackets package exposes is_bracket (already implemented) and a stub is_balanced(s). Implement is_balanced(s) so that it returns True when the three kinds of brackets (), [] and {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, and False otherwise. Characters that are not brackets are ignored. The empty string is balanced. is_balanced must return a bool. Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change is_bracket or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: nested mixed brackets with other characters are balanced: '(a[b]{c})', 'f(x[0], y[1])'
non-bracket characters are ignored
is_balanced returns a bool
TypeError when s is not a string

spec.restated_task: Implement the existing is_balanced(s) stub in brackets/core.py, retaining its availability through from brackets import is_balanced. For string inputs, determine whether all ASCII parentheses, square brackets, and braces match by kind and are properly nested, ignoring every other character. Return an actual bool, treat empty strings and strings without brackets as balanced, and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve is_bracket and the existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept str instances, including subclasses. Process the six characters ()[]{} in their string order, ignoring all other characters. Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket by kind; no opening brackets may remain unmatched at the end. Return True exactly when these conditions hold and False otherwise. The return type must be bool.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str, including bytes, None, numbers, lists, and other iterables. Do not coerce inputs to strings. Exception message is unspecified.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation: return True exactly when c is a str instance of length one containing one of ()[]{}; return False otherwise, including for non-string inputs.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket both succeed.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
4. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}', and '())'.
5. Unmatched openings of every kind are rejected: '[', '{', '(()', and '([]' return False.
6. Unmatched or premature closings of every kind are rejected: ']', '}', ')(', '][', and '}{' return False.
7. Arbitrary valid nesting and concatenation are supported; '((()))', '[[]]', '{{}}', and '([]){}[()]' return True.

8. Every character outside ()[]{} is ignored, including whitespace, newlines, Unicode characters, quotes, and backslashes. Removing all such characters from any input does not change its result; there is no quoting or escaping syntax.
9. Strings without any of the six bracket characters, including 'abc', ' \t\n', and '你好（）', return True.
10. For every string input, type(is_balanced(s)) is bool, including inputs producing False.
11. is_balanced raises TypeError for None, True, 0, 1.5, b'()', [], (), {}, and iter(['(', ')']), rather than returning a result or coercing the input.
12. Instances of a str subclass with ordinary inherited string behavior are accepted and evaluated by the same matching rules.
13. Repeated calls are independent: evaluating '(', then '()', then ')', then '' returns False, True, False, True.
14. is_bracket remains unchanged: each character in '()[]{}' returns True; 'a', '', '((', and 1 return False; all existing tests continue to pass.
15. Existing test files remain unchanged.
out_of_scope: Changing the bracket alphabet or the existing PAIRS, OPEN, and CLOSE definitions.
Adding quoting, escaping, language parsing, or Unicode bracket matching.
Adding dependencies or new public APIs.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception raised in the code under test is never overridden (only a test-internal crash or a timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.
